digest.component_or_area: completion verifier context assembly and recovery
propositions: The completion verifier performs 84-158 read_file/search_files requests per run due to discovering files agentically; 67-82% of these reads are covered by the ticket's declared file_impact union, indicating substantial re-fetching of already-known files.

Pre-fetching the ticket's declared file_impact contents and referencing-commit diffs into the fenced verifier context reduces the request count by 20%+ (live A/B: f6fc 56% reduction, e6a0 30% reduction) while maintaining equal verdict class, with no runaway-loop regressions.

The prefetch mechanism must honor the close gate's graph=False boundary (prefetch only the closing ticket's own file_impact, not subtree descendants) while enabling graph=True deep-review to prefetch a ranked subtree union bounded by a 30k-token aggregate cap and per-file skeleton compression.

The prefetch section is opt-in via an explicit parameter to the shared assemble_context function, defaulting to None so generic review callers like _review_ticket_impl produce byte-identical output and skip prefetch injection.

Recovery successors receive the prefetch via the shared assembled ticket_context at fixed system_prompt positions, where prefetch bytes are included in physical_context_ceiling accounting so oversized prefetch is trimmed rather than raising an error.

The trusted anti-anchoring guidance (confirm prefetch bodies against working tree; re-read skeleton-marked files) resides in the static system-prompt prefix before the volatile marker so it is inherited by both primary verifier and recovery successors, co-located with the prefetch data on both paths.
